## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4ca18be6c30c39bf186d02c68236d79b3af1af4a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/25082-notification-template-hole-placement.md, packages/services/service-messaging/src/template-hole-placement.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/notification-template-placement.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/template-renderer.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/messaging-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/notification-template.object.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/template-hole-placement.test.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/notification-template-placement.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/text-field-html-outlets.pin.test.ts + packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (registerHook / unregisterHooksByPackage, the by-id and per-row `beforeUpdate` dispatch, `insertMany`), packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/core/src/kernel.ts, packages/types/src/validation-failure.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`updateManyData`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/grant-permission-set-name.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml (Check Changeset), AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist 3), .changeset/24983-template-channel-refusal.md, .changeset/25061-notification-template-html-escape.md

Face: narrowing, declared `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset. Inputs: card #25082 (body, every comment; ruling `6335348115` items 2 to 4 govern), PR #25258 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the base `6bc8cc6a`), the 41 check-runs on this head (every one `success` or `skipped`; nothing failed or is pending). Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run. Abstract under the disclosure ruling on #9387 (`5323310017`): placements are named by class only.

### ① Derived judgments

**A. The accept set of `sys_notification_template` writes narrows — right, and exactly as ruled.** A write that leaves a row whose `format` is `html` or `mjml` with a hole outside element text or a quoted plain-text attribute value is refused. The judge is derived from the renderer's one encoder (`escapeHtml` in `template-renderer.ts`: the five markup characters become references, nothing else changes), and that encoding is correct in exactly the two admitted placements. Verified against the renderer at the head: `isHtmlFormat` is the renderer's own test (strict equality on the two spellings, no case folding, so the rows judged are exactly the rows encoded), and `templateHoles` reads the renderer's own `TOKEN`, so the spans judged are the spans substituted (the parity test replays `renderNotification` byte for byte over a corpus that includes non-hole brace pairs).

**B. Fail-closed under every parser reading the judge claims to fork — right.** I walked the scan against the HTML tokenizer and tree-builder rules rather than taking the module note on trust:
- Tokenizer states (data, tag open, end-tag open, tag name, the attribute-name and attribute-value states, self-closing, markup declaration, comment with its abrupt and bang closers, bogus comment, raw / escapable text and their end-tag recognition, plaintext) match the specification's transitions on every character that can move a hole. Every state other than `data`, escapable text, and a double- or single-quoted value on a non-end tag yields a refused class. A hole that lands where it could complete a closing tag or sits in a tag outside any value is refused as `tag`.
- The raw / escapable element set is the specification's (script, style, xmp, iframe, noembed, noframes, noscript; title, textarea; plaintext never left). The fork at a `noscript` start tag (scripting off in a mail client reads it as markup) and at every raw / escapable start tag once a `select` or `frameset` has opened (the tree builder may ignore the start tag, or — for `textarea` in `select` — close the select and honour it) refuses under the conjunction of both readings; a text reading rejoins the markup reading at the end tag, and the `select` / `frameset` flag is never cleared, which only refuses more. The `script` comment-escape handling refuses until the closer and does not model the double-escaped sub-states, which again only refuses more.
- Foreign content: from an `svg` or `math` start tag that is not self-closed, every later hole is refused; a self-closed root opens none, which is what the tree builder does. Integration points and breakout tags are not modelled, so a hole a parser would place back in HTML text is still refused — over-refusal, never admission.
- Readings above the cap mark every later hole refused. No path through the scan admits a hole a parser could place outside the two encoded contexts.

**C. Is anything the judge ADMITS unsafe? No, under the ruling's criterion (encoding by context).** The admitted set is element text (including the two escapable-text elements, where the encoder's reference-encoding is the right encoding) and a quoted value on an attribute that is not read as a URL, a URL list, a handler, a style sheet, markup, or a meta element setting. I checked the URL table against the current and legacy URL-bearing attributes a mail client acts on (href, src, srcset, imagesrcset, action, formaction, cite, data, poster, background, longdesc, usemap, codebase, classid, archive, code, profile, manifest, icon, ping, lowsrc, dynsrc, datasrc, itemtype, itemid, xmlns, every namespaced attribute, and the plugin parameter value); the event-handler prefix and the style attribute are matched after lower-casing; every attribute of a meta element is refused as a class of its own. What remains admitted (class, id, title, alt, width, data-*, target, rel, type, and the like) is text the encoder makes inert in a quoted value. One class the ruling's words do not reach is left admitted: a quoted attribute whose value selects a document setting on a non-meta element (an iframe's sandbox or allow list, a base target). The encoder is correct for it — a value cannot leave the quotes — and a value there changes a setting rather than becoming markup, so it is a semantic choice of the author, not an encoding gap; mail clients do not honour those elements. Named here so it is not read as missed.

**D. Judged over the merged record on every engine write path — right, verified in the engine.** `beforeInsert` dispatches once per row with `input.data` (the array form and `insertMany` route through the same `insert`); a row naming no `format` is judged with the object's declared default (markdown, so not judged — right). `beforeUpdate` carries `previous` on the by-id path (the prior read the engine already does) and on the per-row dispatch of a predicate update (ADR-0058 Addendum II; `hasHooksFor` is per object, so this registration triggers it), the unscoped `multi: true` form included. The hook overlays only defined keys, so a key carried as `undefined` leaves the stored value standing and `body: null` clears the holes (right). The engine has no hook-skipping switch, so system-context writes are judged too, as the PR states; the object's `channel_renders_template` rule is the precedent for that stance. A stored violating row is refused on any edit that leaves it violating, and is still read, listed, deleted, loaded by `NotificationTemplateStore` and rendered unchanged (pinned on a real ObjectQL / SqlDriver; nothing runs at send; no row rewritten). Frozen, not bricked — ruling item 4.

**E. The envelope — right, no new error code.** `validationFailure` (the `@objectstack/types` constructor both HTTP doors map) with one finding at `body`, `code: 'invalid_value'`, `label` from the field declaration; `mapDataError` answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` (pinned); the import runner builds the row report from `fields[0]` (`field: 'body'`, `code: 'invalid_value'`, message head within the 300-character cut, with the refused hole and the way out placed first — right); `updateManyData` carries `VALIDATION_FAILED` / `httpStatus: 400` on the failed record while the other record lands (pinned); a predicate update over a set holding such a row writes no row (pinned). The message names up to five holes with their placement class then counts the rest, names the two supported placements, and sends a link-from-value to `email_template` — ruling item 2's "naming the placement and the supported ones".

**F. Hooks bind and unbind — right.** `bindTemplateHolePlacement` refuses a double (returns `false`) when no `registerHook` exists, unbinds first so a re-bind replaces rather than stacks, and registers both events under one `packageId` scoped to the object at priority 30 (the plugin-security grant-name precedent's shape). `unregisterHooksByPackage` in the engine filters that `packageId` out of every event. The plugin binds in `init` after `ctx.getService('objectql')` — the objectql plugin is a declared dependency and registers that service in its own init, so the engine is present at that point; `destroy()` (which the kernel calls on shutdown, in reverse order) unbinds and clears the reference. Pinned on a booted kernel: refused after bootstrap, accepted after `destroy()`. When the service is absent or has no registry the plugin warns and runs without the check — a fail-open by design for an embedder without ObjectQL, stated in the PR body; flagged under ③.

**G. Public surface — unchanged (right).** `index.ts` is a named export list (no `export *`) and is not in the diff, so the new module exports (`templateHoles`, `isHtmlFormat`, `TemplateHole`, the judge, the hook binders) are package-internal. The outlet census pin lists the two new files as non-outlets with their reason — right, they render nothing. The object docblock gains the rule; no field, index, rule or default changes, so the object's declared shape is unchanged.

**H. Tests — the claims are pinned, not asserted.** 74 unit cases cover both supported placements, every refused class (and the label table's completeness against the closed type), element closing, the comment and declaration edge states, reconsumed characters, the foreign-content, noscript and select / frameset readings, the renderer's grammar and span parity; 20 integration cases cover both doors, import, bulk, predicate, stored-row freeze and repair, read / delete / render, and the plugin's bind / unbind. Test bodies carry holes and markup only, never a value.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-messaging: patch`, with the `**BREAKING**` banner, the `!` summary and PR title, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset, and one ADR-0087 marker: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. This is exactly what the ruling orders ("`patch` with the BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition (#25105 A); `Metadata-protocol: none` under A2") and what AGENTS.md's Post-Task Checklist 3 now states: a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING carriers. The two sibling changesets on this object (`24983`, `25061`) shipped `minor` under the earlier launch-window convention; `patch` is the current rule, so the difference is the rule moving, not this PR. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: the rows are admin-authored data on a platform object, not metadata; no spec key, accepted value, metadata type or default moves. The disposition's category is right on the facts (no ADR-0087 conversion reaches a stored data row; the remedy is the author's edit of a row), and its body carries no arrowed FROM → TO mapping, so the gate's prescription detector is not contradicted; `Check Changeset` (which runs the ADR-0087 registration gate and the no-major guard) is `success` on this head. The `Clause-②:` line is right: nothing widens (no new export, no new accepted value, no new door), and the narrowing is the one the ruling ordered, nothing more.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev report `6347340972`: `open_questions: []`.** Nothing to escalate from the build. The measuring pass's F1 to F4 (`6334219164`) are answered by ruling `6335348115` and this PR follows items 2 to 4 (F2 / B3 is #25190, F1 / A2 is #25189, both outside this PR by the ruling's own split).
- **Deviation: harness-pinned branch `claude/project-thread-iydt23`, not `claude/issue-25082-…`.** The claim comment `6345584878` is the identity record; the closing-target claim guard is `success` on this head. Answered.
- **Deviation: a fourth relay write (`pr_request_reviewers`).** Process, not code; noted.
- **Ruling item 3's "five non-production bodies the build corrects".** All in-tree bodies placing a hole in a URL attribute are email-template bodies (plugin-email's built-ins and the dogfood email-template fixture); there is no html or mjml `sys_notification_template` row anywhere in the tree, so none of the five belongs to this half — they are #25189's. Answered; nothing owed here.
- **Ruling item 3's raw-hole shape.** This face has no raw hole form and no declared variable typing, so no URL hole can be admitted; the refusal routes link-from-value to `email_template`, which has both. Consistent with the ruling, not stricter in any way an author can meet differently.
- **Vocabulary parity with the email half.** The PR adds one class (`meta-attribute`) to the shared class names; the email half (#25212, draft) is not on `main`, so parity is owed by whichever lands second. The dev's out-of-scope note (the email half models fewer readings in two classes) is carried on #25189. Not this PR's to fix.
- **Fail-open without a hook registry.** An embedder whose `objectql` service is absent or exposes no `registerHook` gets a `warn` and no judging. In-tree every kernel composition registers ObjectQL; the PR body states the behaviour. Accepted as declared; an embedder reading that log line is told the check is not running.
- **Docs.** Docs Drift Check lists 28 hand-written pages naming touched identifiers; none carries a notification-template html example with a hole in a refused placement (searched the docs tree). No page is falsified by this diff; the object's `body` description still says "Interpreted per `format`", which remains true.
- **Disclosure.** The PR body, the changeset and this record name placements by class only. The test files necessarily spell each class with an inert hole and no value, the same shape PR #25076's tests took under the same ruling.
